extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in arithmetic geometry / number theory familiar with Inter-Universal Teichmüller (IUT) theory
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of definitions, technical conditions, and upper-bound lemmas from a section of Go Yamashita's exposition of IUT (chapter IV) used in the proposed proof of the abc conjecture. Contains definitions (log-shell, holomorphic hull), choices of initial data, and many quantitative bounds (log-volumes, arithmetic divisors, heights).

rubrics_metrics.name: Log-shell Ik
rubrics_metrics.description: For a non-Archimedean local field k, Ik is defined (notation in text) and for a CAF k Ik is the unit ball; Ik is called the log-shell of k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ik is used as the basic integral (log-)structure at a place; it appears inside tensor products defining holomorphic hulls and log-volumes. The text distinguishes non-Archimedean vs CAF (complex/archimedean) cases when defining Ik.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holomorphic hull of a subset A
rubrics_metrics.description: For A contained in a tensor-product module Iv1;...;vn (for places vi over a chosen v_Q), the holomorphic hull of A is defined as the smallest subset containing A of the form ⊕_i a_i O_{L_i} with a_i ∈ O_{L_i} in the natural direct sum decomposition of the topological modules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The holomorphic hull is the minimal 'integral' (over local rings) enlargement of A respecting the direct sum decomposition; used to define the objects whose log-volume is measured. Tensor products are taken as topological modules. This definition underlies subsequent bounds on log-volumes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aut(C)_prim subgroup
rubrics_metrics.description: Aut(C)^{prim} is defined as the subgroup of Aut(C) generated by complex conjugation and multiplication by √-1 (the multiplication by i), and is described as Z/4Z ⋊ {±1} (notation in text: Z=4Z o {±1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subgroup (primitive automorphisms) is used when describing which automorphisms are allowed for permutative/other indeterminacies in holomorphic hulls and log-shell constructions; it restricts the automorphism group considered in certain archimedean analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of initial tuple (F, EF, V_bad_mod, l, V) — general requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A tuple (F = F; EF; V_bad_mod; l; V) is chosen satisfying a list of numbered conditions (1)–(5) below; this tuple is preliminary data for the constructions and lemmas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tuple encodes a number field F (with algebraic closure), an elliptic curve EF with specified automorphism and torsion properties, a finite set V_bad_mod of bad places, a prime l with special primality conditions, and a finite set V of places of a field K related to F. The full notion of 'initial (Θ)-data' will add more objects/conditions (see referenced Definition 10.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-data condition (1): Field F and algebraic closure
rubrics_metrics.description: F is a number field such that √-1 ∈ F, and F is an algebraic closure (text: 'F is a number field such that (cid:0)1 2 F, and F is an algebraic closure of F').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition fixes basic field-theoretic properties required for later symmetry/automorphism arguments; presence of i ensures certain automorphisms exist inside F.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-data condition (2): Elliptic curve EF properties
rubrics_metrics.description: EF is an elliptic curve over F with Aut_F(EF) = {±1}; the 2:3:5 (=30)-torsion points EF[2:3:5] are rational over F; and F is Galois over the field of moduli F_mod of EF (so there is a short exact sequence 1 → Aut_F(EF) → Aut(EF) → Gal(F/F_mod) → 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These requirements ensure control over automorphisms, level structures, and Galois descent of torsion points; they are used repeatedly in arguments about independence of certain extensions from model choices and Galois properties of associated fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-data condition (3): Non-empty finite V_bad_mod with multiplicative reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: V_bad_mod is a non-empty finite subset of V_mod (V(F_mod)), satisfying that for each v in V_bad_mod the valuation v satisfies certain inequalities (text indicates 'v - 2 holds for each v in V_bad') and EF has bad multiplicative reduction over V_bad_mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This selects bad places where EF has multiplicative reduction; these places contribute q-parameters and are tracked in arithmetic divisors q_L and f_L later. The non-emptiness and finiteness ensure nontrivial contributions to the divisor sums used in bounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-data condition (4): Prime l and primeness constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: l is a prime (l ≥ 5) such that l is prime to elements of V_bad_mod and prime to ord_w of the q-parameters of EF at w in V(F)bad; i.e., l avoids certain local invariants (also 2l is prime to elements in Supp(q_L)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The primality constraints on l (and l ≥ 5) are used to guarantee tameness, unipotent actions on torsion, and to apply level-structure/moduli arguments (properness of X(r) for r≥3). Often l is chosen large enough relative to other invariants to make several inequalities valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial-data condition (5): Set V of places and bijection with V_mod
rubrics_metrics.description: V is a finite subset V ⊂ V(K) (where K := F(EF[l])) such that the natural surjection V(K) → V_mod restricts to a bijection V → V_mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This condition provides a chosen lift (analytic section) of the places V_mod into the valuations of K; the bijection is used to compare normalized degrees and to identify sums over V with sums over V_mod in volume/degree calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of arithmetic divisors d_L, log(d_L), q_L, f_L and log(q_L)
rubrics_metrics.description: For an intermediate extension L (Galois over F_mod) define d_L ∈ ADiv(L) as the effective arithmetic divisor supported in V(L)^non determined by the different ideal of L over Q. Define log(d_L) := (1/[L:Q]) deg_L(d_L). Define q_L ∈ ADiv_R(L) as the effective R-arithmetic divisor (supported in V(L)^non) determined by the q-parameters of EF_L at primes in V(F_L)^bad, divided by ramification indices; define f_L as the effective arithmetic divisor with support Supp(q_L) but coefficients all 1. Log(q_L) := (1/[L:Q]) deg_L(q_L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These divisors and their normalized logs are the principal arithmetic invariants that appear in the quantitative bounds. log(q_L) is independent of choice of L; f_L marks the support (places) of q_L ignoring multiplicities and is used in combinatorial/logarithmic estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of distinguished places V(L)_dist
rubrics_metrics.description: For an intermediate extension L (Galois over F_mod) the set of distinguished places V(L)_dist ⊂ V(L)^non consists of w for which there exists v in V(K)^non with specified ramification/identification properties (text: 'there is v in V(K)^non which is ramified over Q_p etc'). The text describes mapping distinguished places through natural surjections to V_Q and V_mod.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: V_dist singles out places where ramification or other special arithmetic behavior occurs; they appear in Lemma 1.9 and subsequent upper bounds where contributions from distinguished places are non-zero while outside distinguished places volumes vanish.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.7 properties for (F, EF) and related fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims: (1) F_tpd := F_mod(E_{F_mod}[2]) is independent of the model EF_mod; (2) EF has at most semistable reduction for all w ∈ V(F)^non; (3) any model of EF over F with all 3-torsion points defined over F is isomorphic to EF over F; in particular EF_tpd is isomorphic to a model over F_tpd with 3-torsion defined; (4) the extension K/F_mod is Galois.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These structural facts are used to control reduction types, torsion behavior, and Galois symmetry in subsequent ramification, q-parameter, and volume estimates. Proof sketches rely on properness of X(r) for r≥3 and properties of automorphism groups of EF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.8: ramification and unramifiedness bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements: The extension F/F_tpd is tamely ramified outside primes 2,3,5; K/F is tamely ramified outside l; K/F_tpd is unramified outside 2,3,5,l and Supp(q_{F_tpd}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These ramification statements come from semistable reduction and unipotent action on torsion points. They are used in Lemma 1.11 and Proposition 1.12 to bound arithmetic invariants (log(d_K), log(s_Q), etc.) in terms of data on F_tpd and the support of q.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of the holomorphic hulls used to define log-volume (Indet types)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fixed v_Q and integers j (1 ≤ j ≤ l−1), consider the holomorphic hull of the union of certain sets: vertical indeterminacy (Indet "), which are tensor-products of local integral structures at tuples v0,...,vj, and horizontal/permutaive indeterminacies (Indet !, Indet_xy) which run through automorphisms of finite-dimensional Q_{v_Q}-vector spaces inducing automorphisms of submodules I_{v0;...;vj}. The log-volume (j log(...)) is the log-volume of this holomorphic hull.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sets up the geometric object whose log-volume is being bounded. The indeterminacy types correspond to vertical vs horizontal arrows in log-theta-lattices (theta-links vs log-links) and to permutative symmetries of the étale picture. The precise holomorphic hull depends on whether v_Q is non-archimedean, archimedean, or in the distinguished set.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.9: upper bounds for log-volume at a place v_Q
rubrics_metrics.description: Given v_Q ∈ V_Q and tuple-length j (1 ≤ j ≤ l−1), upper bounds of j·log(…) for the holomorphic hulls are provided: (1) for v_Q in V_dist_Q there is an explicit bound involving 2l·ord(q_{v_j}), d_I, (d_I+1)log p_{v_Q}, log(q_{v_j}) normalized by local degrees, log(d_{K_{v_i}}), log(s_{Q_v_Q}), (l+1) factors and additive terms 4(j+1)·log(d_mod^3 l) etc; (2) for v_Q in V_non^Q  ackslash V_dist_Q the log-volume is 0; (3) for v_Q in V_arc^Q the log-volume is ≤ (j+1) log(constant) (text: (j+1) log((cid:25))).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The lemma explains which places contribute and how contributions are measured: distinguished non-archimedean places contribute via q-parameters/ramification and local degrees; non-distinguished non-archimedean places contribute nothing; archimedean places give an explicit finite bound depending only on archimedean norms and dimension (j+1). The lemma references Lemma 1.6 inclusions and uses bounds on e_i, d_mod, and other explicit constants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.10: procession normalised average and global local-average bounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines a weighted average (j log((...))_{v_Q;j}) over (j+1)-tuples of elements of (V_mod)_{v_Q} with weights w_v := [(F_mod)_v : Q_{v_Q}], sums W, and then defines the procession-normalised average (j log((...))_{v_Q}). The lemma gives bounds: (1) for v_Q ∈ V_dist_Q an explicit bound: (l+1)/24·log(q_{v_Q}) + (l+5)/4 ·[terms involving log(d_K_{v_Q}), log(s_Q_{v_Q}), (l+5)log(s_{(…)} ) log(d_mod^3 l)]; (2) for v_Q ∉ V_dist_Q the average is 0; (3) for v_Q archimedean the average ≤ l+1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The weighted averaging normalises contributions across choices of lifts of places to V(K); the lemma aggregates the local bounds of Lemma 1.9 into average bounds used to derive global inequalities. Explicit combinatorial factors (like (l+1)/24) arise from counting arguments and bounding sums over (j+1)-tuples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.11: bounds of global invariants log(d_K), log(s_Q), log(s_{(mod l)})
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides inequalities: (1) log(d_K) ≤ log(d_{F_tpd}) + log(f_{F_tpd}) + 2 log l + 21; (2) log(s_Q) ≤ 2 d_mod (log(d_{F_tpd}) + log(f_{F_tpd})) + log l + 5; (3) there exists a constant prm>0 (from prime number theorem) such that log(s_{(mod l)}) ≤ (4/3)(d_mod·(mod l) + prm) (text gives a more explicit relation using prime number theorem to bound log(s_{(mod l)} ) in terms of d_mod).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These bounds reduce invariants attached to the large extension K and combinatorial counting s(·) to invariants of the smaller field F_tpd and f_{F_tpd}. The proof uses tame ramification, multiplicativity of differents, prime-counting estimates and elementary inequalities log 2<1, log 3<2, log 5<2 etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposition 1.12: global upper bound for j·log((...)) and consequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sets j log(q)_j := (1/2l) log(q) (global average) and proves an explicit global upper bound for (1) j log((…)) := ∑_{v_Q ∈ V_Q} j log((…))_{v_Q}, namely an inequality of the form j log((…)) ≤ (1/(2l)) log(q) + (1/6)·(l+1)/4·[ (1 + 12 d_mod / l) (log(d_{F_tpd}) + log(f_{F_tpd})) + 10(d_mod^3 l + prm) ]. In particular j log((…)) < 1, and if j log(q)_j ≥ j log((…)) then a lower bound on log(q) in terms of log(d_{F_tpd}) + log(f_{F_tpd}) and d_mod appears (explicit constants provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the principal global quantitative inequality: it aggregates local average bounds and the bounds on global invariants to compare a normalized log(q) to the constructed log-volume j log((…)). The 'in particular' statement gives the smallness of j log((…)) (<1) and a criterion (if average log(q) exceeds the bound) forcing log(q) to be large in terms of arithmetic invariants. Constants depend on l, d_mod and a constant prm from prime number theory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Faltings height ht_Falt for semi-abelian varieties (relative dimension 1)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a semi-abelian variety E of relative dimension 1 over Spec O_F with generic fiber EF an elliptic curve, the Faltings height ht_Falt(E) is defined as (1/[F:Q]) deg_F(ω_E) where ω_E is the module of invariant differentials equipped with an Arakelov (Hermitian) metric at archimedean places (the metric jj·jj_Falt described in text). The non-archimedean and archimedean contributions are given explicitly: the non-archimedean part equals (1/[F:Q]) log # (ω_E / a ω_E) for a ∈ ω_E and the archimedean part involves integrals over E_v(~ complex normalization).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard arithmetic-geometric definition is used to compare different height functions (ht_{!P1} and ht_Falt) and to derive inequalities in Lemma 1.13. The metric variation across UP1(C) and the behavior near cusps (0,1,∞) are important; the archimedean metric has logarithmic singularities at the cusps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lemma 1.13: relations between ht_{!P1(f0;1;1g)} and ht_Falt and behavior under isogeny
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements: (1) For any ε>0 on UP1(Q): 2 ht_Falt ≲ ht_{!P1(f0;1;1g)} ≲ 2 ht_Falt + log(ht_{!P1(f0;1;1g)}) ≲ 2 ht_Falt + O_ε(ht_{!P1(f0;1;1g)}^ε) (text gives inequalities 2ht_Falt . ht_{!P1} . 2ht_Falt + log(ht_{!P1}) . 2ht_Falt + ε ht_{!P1}); (2) For H⊂E[l] cyclic of order l, ht_Falt([E;(θ)]) − (1/2) log l ≤ ht_Falt([E/H; Im(θ)]) ≤ ht_Falt([E;(θ)]) + (1/2) log l; (3) Under the additional assumption that l is prime to the local v(q_{E;v}), the non-archimedean part satisfies l · htnon_{!P1}([E;(θ)]) = htnon_{!P1}([E/H; Im(θ)]).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These relations compare the modular height ht_{!P1(f0;1;1g)} (on the UP1-line) with Faltings height and quantify how heights change under quotient by a cyclic subgroup of order l. The equality for non-archimedean parts under primeness assumptions is especially important in the descent/averaging arguments used in IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archimedean vs non-archimedean contributions and singularity behavior of metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: The archimedean metric jj·jj_Falt on ω_E varies continuously on UP1(C) but has logarithmic singularities at the cusps {0,1,∞}; near a cusp the local behavior is governed by q-parameters with Im(τ)-type expressions and yields explicit logarithmic terms in ht_Falt(E;dz)_arc. Non-archimedean contributions are given by sums over v∈V(F)^non of normalized valuations times log q_v.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This observation explains why ht_{!P1(f0;1;1g)} has logarithmic singularity and how the non-archimedean height equals certain normalized sums of log q_v; used to relate modular heights and Faltings heights and to bound their difference.
